text: A day on Mars is called a sol. It lasts 24 hours and 39 minutes.
Mars gets less than half the sunlight Earth gets, so solar panels make less Power there.
Mars has a lumpy little moon called Phobos. It is only about 27 km long.
You played in Jezero Crater, where NASA's Perseverance rover landed. Scientists think it held a lake about 3.5 billion years ago.
NASA's Curiosity rover has a radiation detector on Mars. In {radiationPeriod} it checked the radiation {radiationReadings} times!
This map is a real place: Jezero Crater on Mars! It is about 45 km wide, and long ago it held a lake.
Solar flares are sorted by letters. An X flare is 10 times stronger than an M flare, and 100 times stronger than a C flare.
source: NASA Science: What is a solar flare?

text: In 2018 a dust storm on Mars grew so big it wrapped around the whole planet. It blocked the sunlight NASA's Opportunity rover used for power.
Mars is freezing at night! Where the Viking 1 lander sat, it got as cold as -89 °C.
A radio message between Earth and Mars takes 3 to 22 minutes, so astronauts must plan ahead.
Astronauts grow lettuce on the International Space Station in a little garden called Veggie, and they get to eat it!
You can't see space radiation, but NASA calls it one of the most dangerous parts of space travel. That's why your base needs a Shield!
Radiation is real on Mars: NASA's Curiosity rover measures it there every day. A thick Shield keeps your crew safe.
